questions.heading: SAIFI Counts Interruptions and SAIDI Counts Minutes, per Customer Served
questions.stem: A utility serving 50,000 customers has two outages in a year: 2,000 customers out for 90 minutes, and 10,000 customers out for 3 minutes. What are its SAIFI and SAIDI?

options.text: SAIFI 0.24 and SAIDI 4.2, since every customer who lost power is counted once
options.says: The 3-minute outage is momentary; only interruptions over five minutes count in either index.

options.text: SAIFI 0.04 and SAIDI 3.6, since the shorter outage is momentary and left out
options.says: Right: 2,000 / 50,000 = 0.04 and 2,000 x 90 / 50,000 = 3.6; the 3-minute outage counts in neither.

options.text: SAIFI 1.0 and SAIDI 90, since each index divides by the customers interrupted
options.says: Both divide by all customers served; dividing by those interrupted is CAIDI's denominator.

options.text: SAIFI 0.04 and SAIDI 4.2, since the shorter outage adds minutes but not interruptions
options.says: A momentary interruption is left out of SAIDI as well as SAIFI.

questions.heading: Expected Failures Avoided Turn Into Every Non-Financial Measure
questions.stem: A tower replacement avoids 0.25 expected failures over the window. One failure of that tower cuts off 8,000 customers for 150 minutes. How many customer-minutes of interruption does the project avoid?

options.text: 1,200,000, since a failure the project prevents is one that would surely happen
options.says: 0.25 is an expected count; the measure multiplies it in rather than assuming a whole failure.

options.text: 2,000, since the customers count here and the minutes belong to SAIDI alone
options.says: Customer-minutes are customers times minutes; 2,000 is the customer interruptions avoided.

options.text: 37.5, since the minutes count here and the customers belong to SAIFI alone
options.says: Customer-minutes need both factors: the customers cut off and how long they wait.

options.text: 300,000, since a fraction of a failure still brings its customers times its minutes

questions.heading: Financial Benefit Is NPV, and Each Consequence Is Counted Once
questions.stem: A utility's NPV for a pole replacement includes the emergency repair bills the work saves. An analyst proposes adding 'repair cost avoided, $k' as a fifth measure beside NPV. What should the value function do?

options.text: Leave it out, since those dollars sit inside NPV and would carry weight twice
options.says: Right: the same consequence counted twice gets twice the weight it deserves.

options.text: Add it, since repair cost and NPV are correlated measures of separate things
options.says: Correlated measures of separate consequences are fine, but here it is the same money, not a separate consequence.

options.text: Add it, since a measure stated in $k joins NPV without any weight of its own
options.says: Every measure gets its own reference and weight; sharing a unit does not make it a different consequence.

options.text: Add it, since the board can lower NPV's weight to make up for the overlap
options.says: An overlap is removed before options are compared, not patched with a weight.
